tasks.prompt: Order the start-up checks for a new duplex lift station before it is placed in automatic service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: newly constructed duplex submersible lift station, from document review through automatic operation.

cards.label: Fill the wet well with clean water and test each float level for pump start, pump stop, and high level alarm
Run the duty pump on a timed drawdown and record the pumping rate and any abnormal noise or vibration
Confirm pump rotation, valve positions, and discharge piping by a brief manual run of each pump
Place the station in automatic, confirm the standby pump alternates, and record the start-up results in the station log
Inspect the wet well to confirm it is clean, free of construction debris, and the discharge valves are in the correct position
Review approved drawings, approvals, and the operations manual for the station

tasks.explanation: Documents and a clean, correctly valved wet well come before any pump run. Float and alarm testing with clean water proves the controls before sewage arrives, the timed drawdown proves capacity, and automatic operation with alternation is confirmed last and logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the return to service of a lift station after an extended shutdown for wet well repairs.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: duplex lift station taken out of service for two weeks, repairs complete, sewage held upstream by a plug and bypass pumping on standby.

cards.label: Ventilate the wet well area and test the atmosphere before any work at the open wet well
Inspect the wet well level, pumps, floats, and discharge valves for correct position and freedom of movement
Confirm the repair work is complete and the work area is clear of tools, plugs are accounted for, and the supervisor authorizes return to service
Restore electrical power and remove lockout devices following the lockout procedure, with all workers clear
Return the controls to automatic, confirm float operation through one full cycle, and stand down the bypass pumping
Run each pump manually one at a time and confirm discharge flow, check valve operation, and no leaks

tasks.explanation: Authorization and a clear work area come first, then atmospheric safety, then mechanical inspection. Power is restored only under the lockout procedure, manual runs prove each pump before automatic control is trusted, and bypass pumping is stood down only after a full automatic cycle is proven.

tasks.prompt: Order the float and alarm proving test during a lift station start-up.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: clean water test of a duplex station with stop, lead start, lag start, and high level floats in one wet well.

cards.label: Restore normal alternation, return levels to normal, and record every proven setpoint in the start-up record
Confirm the lead pump starts at its start float level and note the level
Raise the clean water level slowly with all pumps in automatic and the alarm system active
Confirm the lead pump stops at the stop float level as the level is drawn down, and note the level
Raise the level further to confirm the high level alarm activates and is received at the monitoring point
Block the lead pump off and raise the level to confirm the lag pump starts at its higher start level

tasks.explanation: Setpoints are proven in the order the levels occur in service, from normal start and stop through lag start to high level alarm. Recording proven setpoints and restoring normal alternation closes the test.

tasks.prompt: Order the standby generator proving steps at a lift station during commissioning.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: new lift station with an automatic standby generator and transfer switch, tested before the station enters service.

cards.label: Simulate a utility power failure at the transfer switch so the generator starts and accepts the station load automatically
Record the test results and deficiencies in the commissioning record and station log
Restore utility power, confirm automatic transfer back and generator cooldown and shutdown
Run the generator unloaded and confirm voltage, frequency, and no alarms
Confirm fuel, coolant, oil, battery, and block heater status are satisfactory on the generator inspection
Run the station pumps under generator power and record load, run time, and any alarms

tasks.explanation: Static checks come before running, unloaded running proves the machine, and only then is a simulated outage used to prove automatic transfer under real pump load. Transfer back, cooldown, and records complete the proving test.

tasks.prompt: Order the pre-start checks before the first sewage is admitted to a new lift station wet well.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: clean water testing is complete, upstream gravity sewer is ready to be connected to the new station.

cards.label: Confirm clean water test records are complete and all start-up deficiencies are corrected and signed off
Remove test water, plugs, and temporary equipment from the wet well and confirm the influent valve or stop logs are ready to open
Confirm communications, alarm dialer or SCADA points, and the high level alarm have been received at the monitoring station
Admit sewage by opening the influent in a controlled manner while watching the first automatic pump cycles
Record the in-service date, initial readings, and any issues in the station log and notify operations staff the station is live
Confirm standby power, spare pump parts, and the emergency response contact list are in place at the station

tasks.explanation: A station is not put live on hope. Signed off testing, a clear wet well, proven alarms and communications, and support in place all precede admitting sewage, and the first cycles are watched and logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the checks when starting a portable bypass pump to hold a lift station wet well during repairs.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: engine driven bypass pump set up at a lift station, suction in the wet well and discharge to the force main through a temporary connection.

cards.label: Record start time, levels, and fuel status in the log and brief the incoming operator on refuelling and alarm response
Confirm the high level alarm and level watch arrangements are active for the bypass period and assign the monitoring rotation
Start the pump and confirm it holds the wet well level below the alarm level without surging or losing prime
Install the suction hose in the wet well and the discharge connection, and confirm all couplings and check valves are correct
Set up traffic control and barriers and position the bypass pump on stable ground with the discharge hose secured
Prime the pump and confirm fuel, oil, and coolant are sufficient for the planned run period

tasks.explanation: Safe setup and correct hoses and valves come before priming and starting. The bypass is only proven when it holds the level steadily, and monitoring, alarms, and a documented handover protect the whole bypass period.

tasks.prompt: Order the sequence for placing a newly replaced submersible pump into service in an existing wet well.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: replacement pump lowered onto the guide rails in a duplex station, the other pump has carried the station during the change.

cards.label: Connect power and control cables, restore the breaker, and remove lockout devices under the lockout procedure
Update the asset record and station log with the new pump serial number, date, and test results
Run the pump manually and confirm correct rotation by flow, normal current draw, and no abnormal vibration
Lower the pump on the guide rails and confirm it seats fully on the discharge elbow with the lifting chain secured at the top
Cycle the pump on its floats in automatic and confirm the check valve closes without slam and the level controls respond
Confirm the replacement pump matches the duty, rotation, voltage, and discharge connection of the original

tasks.explanation: Matching and correct seating come before power is restored. Manual running proves rotation and current before float control is trusted, and the asset record is updated so the next operator knows what is installed.

tasks.prompt: Order the wet well cleaning preparation steps before a lift station is started up again after cleaning.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: contract vacuum truck has cleaned the wet well of a duplex station held on bypass pumping.

cards.label: Inspect floats, pump intakes, and the wet well floor from the surface and confirm no damage or leftover debris
Record the cleaning, any defects found, and the return to service in the station log and work order
Confirm cleaning is complete and all vacuum hoses, tools, and workers are clear of the wet well
Remove bypass suction from the wet well in coordination with the vacuum crew and restore normal influent flow
Run each pump manually to confirm free operation and correct discharge before using automatic control
Return the station to automatic and watch one complete fill and drawdown cycle

tasks.explanation: People and equipment clear and a surface inspection come before flow is restored. Manual runs and one watched automatic cycle prove the station before it is left unattended, and the work is documented.

tasks.prompt: Order a routine daily operations round at a small duplex lift station.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: daily attended round, no alarms active, operator records the visit on the station log sheet.

cards.label: Observe one automatic pump cycle and note wet well levels at pump start and stop
Record levels, run hours, starts, and any defects in the log and raise work orders for items needing repair
Check ventilation, heating, lighting, sump, and the standby generator status panel
Check each pump for abnormal noise, vibration, leakage, and discharge pressure where gauges are fitted
Check the station exterior, access, fencing, and any signs of vandalism, overflow, or odour on arrival
Review the alarm history, run hours, and start counters since the last visit before touching any controls

tasks.explanation: The round starts outside and with the recorded history, so the operator knows what changed before operating anything. Observing a real cycle and checking auxiliaries follow, and recording plus work orders close the visit.

tasks.prompt: Order the wet well grease and ragging inspection and surface cleaning routine.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: monthly surface routine at a duplex station, no entry, using a washdown hose and a rake from the top slab.

cards.label: Wash down the walls and floats with the station hose and break up surface grease so pumps can draw it down in small amounts
Review recent run hours and alarms for signs of ragging or grease buildup before opening the wet well cover
Inspect the surface for grease mats, float fouling, and debris around the pump intakes from above
Open the cover, ventilate the headspace, and test the atmosphere at the opening before leaning over the well
Run the pumps to draw the level down and confirm floats move freely through a full cycle
Close and secure the cover and record the condition found and the cleaning done in the station log

tasks.explanation: History first, then safe opening with ventilation and testing before any surface work. Washing and float checks follow, a proven cycle confirms the result, and the log records the condition for trending.

tasks.prompt: Order the monthly CMOM style review of collection system performance records.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: supervisor reviews the month blockages, overflows, cleaning production, and complaint records before the program meeting.

cards.label: Identify repeat locations and check whether their follow up inspections or repairs were completed as scheduled
Review cleaning and CCTV production against the program targets and note the reasons for any shortfall
Record the review decisions and assigned actions in the program file with dates and owners
Select the priority actions for next month, such as hotspot frequency changes, targeted CCTV, or rehabilitation referrals
Compare the counts with previous months and the same month last year to identify trends rather than single events
Compile the month counts for blockages, overflows, backups, and odour complaints by area from the work order system

tasks.explanation: Compiled counts come before interpretation. Trend comparison separates patterns from noise, repeat locations test whether follow up actually happened, production is reviewed against targets, and decisions are recorded with owners and dates so the next review can audit them.

tasks.prompt: Order the manual verification of wet well level against the SCADA reading during a round.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: operator suspects the level transmitter may be drifting at a station with both floats and a level transmitter.

cards.label: If the difference exceeds the site tolerance, tag the reading as suspect, rely on float control, and raise a calibration work order
Raise and lower the level through one pump cycle and confirm the SCADA reading tracks the measured change
Measure the actual level from the fixed reference point on the top slab with a tape or staff gauge
Record the SCADA level reading and the time before going to the wet well
Record both readings, the difference, and the action taken in the station log
Compare the measured level with the SCADA value and note the difference

tasks.explanation: The comparison needs a recorded SCADA value and an independent manual measurement at a known reference. Tracking through a cycle separates a fixed offset from a dead signal, and tagging plus a work order protects operations until calibration.

tasks.prompt: Order the response checks when a lift station round finds one pump with far more run hours than its twin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: duplex alternating station, run hour meters show the duty pump has run about three times the hours of the standby this month.

cards.label: Record findings in the log and raise a work order for any control or check valve defect found
Record both run hour totals and start counts and compare them with the previous round readings
Check the high hour pump discharge check valve for leakage that could be recycling flow back to the well
Force an alternation and observe the next automatic cycle on the previously idle pump
Check the control panel alternator setting and confirm it is in automatic alternation, not locked on one pump
Run the low hour pump manually and confirm it pumps, draws normal current, and its discharge valve is open

tasks.explanation: Data first, then the alternator setting, then proving the idle pump actually works. A leaking check valve on the busy pump is checked because it inflates run hours, and a forced alternation proves the fix before leaving.

tasks.prompt: Order the bar screen and influent channel check at a lift station with a manual screen.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: weekly check of the influent screen basket ahead of the wet well at a small station, no entry required.

cards.label: Record the volume of screenings, condition of the basket, and disposal in the station log
Check flows and wet well behaviour for signs of a blinded screen, such as low inflow with upstream surcharge
Replace the basket fully seated and confirm inflow passes freely into the wet well
Ventilate and test the atmosphere at the screen chamber opening before opening the cover fully
Lift the screen basket clear and empty screenings into the lined container for disposal
Wash the basket and channel, inspect for damage, and check the channel for grit and grease buildup

tasks.explanation: Symptoms are checked first, then the chamber is opened safely. Cleaning, inspection, and correct reseating follow in that order, and free inflow plus a log entry close the task.

tasks.prompt: Order the end of shift handover for a collection operator covering several lift stations.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: day operator hands over to the on call operator for the night, two stations have open items.

cards.label: Pass on keys, the on call phone, radio, and the current confined space and lockout status for any open permits
Sign off the shift record with times, names, and the items transferred
Brief the incoming operator on planned night work, expected high flows, and any customer or spill follow ups pending
Summarize active alarms, bypasses, and any station running on a single pump or manual control
Complete all station logs and work orders for the shift before the handover discussion
Confirm the incoming operator has read and understood the open items and note the handover in the log

tasks.explanation: Records are completed first so the handover is based on written facts. Risks and open items are briefed before equipment and permits change hands, and a signed record proves the transfer.

tasks.prompt: Order a planned manual changeover from the duty pump to the standby pump at a duplex lift station.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: planned changeover for equal wear, both pumps healthy, station in automatic alternation.

cards.label: Record the changeover, the reason, and the new duty assignment in the station log
Place the duty pump control in the off position and confirm it stops and the level begins to rise slowly
Observe one full automatic cycle on the new duty pump and confirm start and stop levels are correct
Return the proven standby pump to automatic as the new duty pump and set the original pump as standby
Place the standby pump in hand and run it to confirm normal flow, current, and discharge before relying on it
Record current wet well level, run hours, and starts for both pumps before making any change

tasks.explanation: Baseline readings come first. The old duty is stopped, the standby is proven in hand before it is trusted in automatic, one full cycle is observed, and the change is logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a high level alarm at a duplex lift station at night.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: on call operator receives a high level alarm by SCADA and dialer, attends the station, no overflow has occurred yet.

cards.label: On arrival check the wet well level and whether either pump is running, and check for any overflow at the station
Acknowledge the alarm, note the time and level trend, and advise the supervisor while travelling to the station
If pumping cannot control the level, arrange bypass pumping and tanker support and notify the supervisor of overflow risk
When the level is normal, restore automatic control, confirm the alarm clears, and complete the alarm response record
Start a pump manually to draw the level down and place the second pump in automatic as backup
Check pump control positions, breakers, and overloads, and identify why the duty pump did not start or did not keep up

tasks.explanation: Acknowledgement and notification start the response. On site, level and overflow status come before control checks, manual pumping restores control, escalation to bypass happens before an overflow if pumping is insufficient, and records close the event.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a pump fail alarm where the tripped pump is found on overload.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: duplex station, one pump tripped on overload, the other pump is holding the level.

cards.label: Check for the cause in order, starting with the wet well for rags or debris at the pump intake from the surface
Reset the overload once only if no fault is found and run the pump briefly in hand while watching current draw
Confirm the standby pump is controlling the level and the station is not at risk before investigating the tripped pump
Isolate the tripped pump electrically and apply lockout before any hands on inspection
Return the pump to automatic if it runs normally, or leave it isolated and raise a repair work order, recording all findings
Check the pump and cable for damage and test the motor as permitted by site procedure before any reset

tasks.explanation: Station safety comes first because the other pump is carrying the load. Lockout precedes inspection, likely causes are checked from simplest to electrical, a single cautious reset follows only a no fault finding, and the outcome is recorded either way.

tasks.prompt: Order the investigation of repeated low level cut out and pump cavitation noise at a lift station.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: operator reports the duty pump runs past its normal stop point, is noisy, and the wet well is drawn very low each cycle.

cards.label: Inspect the stop float from the surface for grease fouling, tangled cable, or a float hanging up on the wall or ladder
Check the second pump stop control the same way and confirm both pumps stop correctly
Clean or free the float as needed and confirm it moves freely through its full travel
Record the observed stop level and compare it with the design stop level and the float positions
Record the cause, the cleaning done, and the verified stop levels in the station log
Run a controlled cycle and confirm the pump now stops at the correct level without cavitation noise

tasks.explanation: The stop level evidence points first to the stop float, the most common cause. Cleaning and freeing it precedes a controlled proving cycle, the twin pump is checked for the same fault, and verified levels are logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a seal fail or high temperature alarm on a submersible pump.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: duplex station, panel shows a seal moisture and winding temperature alarm on one pump, the pump has been stopped by its protection.

cards.label: Arrange lifting of the pump by the approved method and inspect the seal chamber oil or moisture reading as directed by the manufacturer procedure
Decide repair or replacement with the supervisor based on the inspection and keep the pump out of service until cleared
Record the alarm, inspection results, and the out of service status in the log and asset record
Record the alarm type, time, run hours, and recent current readings for the alarmed pump
Isolate and lock out the pump if any lifting or electrical work will be done
Confirm the other pump is controlling the level and place the alarmed pump control in off so it cannot restart

tasks.explanation: The healthy pump carries the station while the alarmed pump is positively prevented from restarting. Protection alarms on seals and windings mean the pump stays out until inspected, because running it risks motor failure and oil release to the flow.

tasks.prompt: Order the lift station response to a utility power failure with a standby generator.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: storm related outage, generator should start automatically, operator attends to confirm station operation.

cards.label: Check generator fuel, oil, coolant, and battery charger status and estimate run time available on the fuel on hand
Arrange refuelling or a portable generator if the outage is expected to exceed the fuel run time
On arrival confirm the generator is running, the transfer switch is in the emergency position, and pumps are cycling normally
Check the wet well level trend and confirm no high level or overflow condition is developing
When utility power returns, confirm transfer back, generator cooldown and shutdown, and record the event times and readings
Confirm the outage and alarm times from SCADA or the dialer and advise the supervisor of the affected station

tasks.explanation: Remote confirmation and notification come first. On site the generator and transfer are verified before auxiliaries and levels, fuel run time drives escalation, and restoration is confirmed and logged when power returns.

tasks.prompt: Order the troubleshooting sequence when a pump runs but the wet well level does not fall.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: duplex station, duty pump motor runs with normal sound but the level keeps rising slowly.

cards.label: Check for a failed check valve or a broken discharge by watching for flow returning to the well when the pump stops
Confirm the pump discharge valve is fully open and the correct valve lineup is in place
Stop the pump and check the wet well intake from the surface for rags or a grease mat blocking the volute
Check the discharge pressure gauge or force main pressure for a reading that suggests pumping against a closed or blocked line
Leave the faulty pump isolated, record the test results, and raise a work order describing which checks were done
Switch duty to the other pump and confirm it draws the level down, isolating the fault to the first pump or its branch

tasks.explanation: Valve lineup is the fastest external check, then pressure, then intake blockage, then return flow. Proving the twin pump narrows the fault to one branch, and the documented checks save the repair crew repeating them.

tasks.prompt: Order the return of a repaired pump to automatic service after maintenance at a lift station.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: pump was isolated and locked out for a seal replacement by the maintenance crew, work is signed complete.

cards.label: Place the pump in automatic and observe it start and stop correctly on its floats through one cycle
Record the return to service, test readings, and the new duty or standby assignment in the station log
Confirm the maintenance work is complete, all workers are clear, and the work permit or job record is signed off
Confirm the pump is seated, cables are secured clear of the floats, and discharge valves are in the normal position
Run the pump in hand and confirm flow, current, rotation, and no leaks or abnormal noise
Remove lockout devices by the persons who applied them, following the lockout procedure

tasks.explanation: Signed off work and controlled lock removal come before power. Seating, cables, and valves are checked before the hand run, automatic float operation is observed, and the return is logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the inspection of an air release valve chamber on a sewage force main.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: scheduled inspection of a combination air valve at the high point of a force main, chamber inspection is from the surface with the cover open, no entry planned.

cards.label: Test the atmosphere at the opening and inspect the valve body, isolating valve position, and chamber for leakage or corrosion from the surface
Set up traffic control or barriers as needed and open the chamber cover with ventilation at the opening
Review the force main operating pressure and confirm which pumps are running before opening the chamber
If the valve is fouled, isolate it by closing the isolating valve and arrange cleaning or replacement under a separate work plan
Close and secure the cover, record the valve condition and pressure, and raise work orders for any defects
Confirm the isolating valve is fully open so the air valve can operate, and note any sewage weeping from the valve outlet

tasks.explanation: Pressure and pump status set the risk picture before the chamber is opened. Safe opening and testing precede inspection, the isolating valve position is critical because a closed valve disables air release, and findings are recorded with follow up work raised.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a suspected force main leak reported as sewage surfacing in a ditch.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: public report of sewage and odour in a roadside ditch along the force main route from a duplex station.

cards.label: Reduce or stop pumping from the lift station in coordination with operations to limit the leak while keeping the wet well from overflowing
Arrange repair, cleanup and disinfection of the affected area, sampling as directed, and complete the spill documentation
Confirm the surfacing liquid is sewage and identify the nearest force main fittings, valves, and low points from the drawings
Excavate or expose the main only under an excavation plan with locates, and confirm the leak location and cause
Contain the surfacing sewage with berms or a vacuum truck to protect the watercourse and prevent spread
Notify the supervisor, record the report details, and attend with spill response equipment and traffic control

tasks.explanation: Notification and containment thinking start immediately. Drawings locate the likely source, pumping is balanced against wet well overflow risk, containment protects the environment before excavation, and repair plus documented cleanup closes the event.

tasks.prompt: Order the controlled refilling and return to service of a force main after a repair.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a section of force main was drained and repaired, the line is empty between the station and the repair point.

cards.label: Start one pump at the station to fill the main slowly and vent air at the high points in a controlled manner
Record the return to service, pressures observed, and any leakage checks in the operations log
Watch pressures as the main fills and check the repair and fittings for leakage as pressure builds
Bring the main to normal operating pressure and run both pumps in turn to confirm normal pressures and flows
Confirm the repair is complete, all fittings and thrust restraints are in place, and the excavation crew is clear for pressurization
Confirm air release valves on the route are in service and discharge isolation valves are correctly positioned

tasks.explanation: A drained main is refilled slowly with air valves in service, because trapped air causes surge and false pressure readings. The repair is checked under rising pressure before full duty, and normal operation on both pumps plus records complete the return.

tasks.prompt: Order the force main valve exercise routine for an isolation valve that is operated infrequently.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: annual exercising of a buried force main isolation valve with a valve key from the surface valve box.

cards.label: Record the date, turns, condition, and any stiffness or leakage in the valve record
Return the valve to its normal fully open position and confirm the turn count matches the expected full travel
Notify operations and confirm the station can run without the affected section or that the valve will only be partially closed
Open the valve box, clean out debris, and confirm the operating nut is intact and accessible
Turn the valve slowly in the closing direction for a few turns, then back, working toward full travel over repeated movements
Review the drawings to confirm the valve location, normal position, and the effect of closing it on station operation

tasks.explanation: Drawings and operational impact come before touching the valve. Exercising is gradual to avoid surge and to free a stiff valve without breaking the stem, the valve is left in its normal position verified by turn count, and the record supports the valve program.

tasks.prompt: Order the investigation of rising force main discharge pressure at a lift station over several weeks.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: discharge pressure at constant flow has risen steadily, suggesting a restriction or air binding in the force main.

cards.label: Compare pump performance against its curve at the measured pressure to separate pump wear from main restriction
Check air release valves on the route are in service and not fouled, since trapped air restricts the main
Check all force main isolation and check valves are fully open and in their normal positions
If the main is restricted, plan cleaning or pigging or internal inspection with the supervisor based on the findings
Record the pressures, checks completed, and the planned action in the station log and work order system
Confirm the trend from logged pressures and flows and rule out a faulty gauge by comparing with a test gauge

tasks.explanation: Data and gauge verification come first so work is not based on a bad instrument. Air valves and valve positions are the common external causes, pump condition is separated from main condition by the curve, and intrusive cleaning is planned only on evidence.

tasks.prompt: Order the safe isolation of a force main section for a planned repair.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: planned repair of a force main fitting, the section must be isolated, drained, and proven safe before the crew opens it.

cards.label: Plan the isolation with operations, including how sewage will be held or bypassed while the station cannot pump to the normal outlet
Stop the station pumps and close and tag the isolation valves at both ends of the work section
Open the drain or low point fitting to drain the section to a vacuum truck or approved point and confirm flow stops
Record the isolation points, tag numbers, and drain confirmation in the work plan and log
Prove the isolation by cracking a test fitting at the work point and confirming no pressure or flow before authorizing opening the main
Open a high point air valve or fitting to break vacuum and confirm the section is fully drained and at atmospheric pressure

tasks.explanation: Planning for held sewage comes before any valve is moved. Double isolation, draining, and venting follow, and the section is proven dead at the work point before anyone opens it, with the isolation documented.

tasks.prompt: Order a manhole inspection from the surface, starting before the cover is removed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: routine condition inspection of a gravity sewer manhole on a residential street, no entry, inspection from the surface.

cards.label: Assess the surface first, noting pavement condition, cover fit and rocking, frame movement, and signs of surcharge or odour
Inspect the frame, chimney, cone, walls, and steps or ladder for cracks, corrosion, infiltration, and displaced joints
Measure or estimate flow depth and condition, photograph defects, and record the inspection on the standard form
Set up traffic control and barriers suited to the road position before opening the cover
Ventilate the manhole headspace and test the atmosphere at the opening before looking into the structure
Inspect the benching and channel for smoothness, deposits, roots, and proper flow guidance through the structure

tasks.explanation: Surface condition tells part of the story before opening. Traffic control and atmospheric safety precede looking inside, the structure is inspected top to bottom ending at the channel where flow performance is judged, and photographs plus the form capture the result.

tasks.prompt: Order the safe opening of a manhole cover in a travelled lane for a short inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: two person crew, manhole in the travelled portion of a two lane road, inspection will take about fifteen minutes.

cards.label: Complete the inspection with one worker acting as watch for traffic while the other works at the opening
Replace and seat the cover, confirm it is flush and stable, then remove traffic control in the reverse order of setup
Position the vehicle as a barrier where the plan requires it and set the remaining cones and buffer space
Place advance warning signs and the cone taper to close or protect the work lane before stopping at the manhole
Open the cover with the correct hook, keeping body position clear of traffic, and place the cover where it cannot be struck
Review the traffic plan for the location and confirm the signs, cones, and flagging arrangements match the road layout

tasks.explanation: Traffic control is fully in place before the cover is touched, and the vehicle and watch protect the open hole. The cover is proven seated before control is removed in reverse order so the road is never left unprotected with an open or loose cover.

tasks.prompt: Order the inspection sequence inside a manhole during a CCTV support role, working from the surface.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: operator at the upstream manhole guides the CCTV camera into the correct pipe while the truck operator is at the downstream manhole.

cards.label: Identify the correct outgoing pipe by channel layout, flow direction, and the drawings, not by assumption
Open the manhole safely with ventilation and atmospheric testing at the opening
Guide the camera or jetter hose into the selected pipe as directed and confirm with the truck operator that it entered the right line
Confirm with the truck operator which pipe run and direction will be inspected and agree the communication signals
Monitor flow and watch for surcharge or debris returning while the inspection proceeds and report changes immediately
When the run is complete, confirm the camera is recovered, replace the cover securely, and record the run details

tasks.explanation: Agreement on the run and signals comes before opening. Correct pipe identification uses the channel, flow, and drawings together, because entering the wrong pipe wastes the inspection. Recovery and records close the support role.

tasks.prompt: Order the measurement of flow depth and estimation of surcharge condition in a manhole.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: capacity complaint investigation, operator measures depth in a trunk sewer manhole during morning peak flow.

cards.label: Measure the flow depth in the channel with a staff gauge or tape from a fixed reference and record the pipe diameter
Open the manhole safely with traffic control, ventilation, and atmospheric testing at the opening
Record the time, weather, and recent rainfall before opening, since depth only has meaning with its conditions
Record depth, pipe size, time, and observations on the inspection form and flag any surcharge evidence for engineering follow up
Note the high water mark evidence on the walls, such as staining or debris, and photograph it with the current level for comparison
Observe the flow for several minutes for surcharging signs such as a rising level, submerged benching, or debris lines above the flow

tasks.explanation: Conditions are recorded first because a depth without time and weather cannot be interpreted. Measurement, observation over time, and high water evidence follow in order, and the form plus flagging turns a reading into usable capacity data.

tasks.prompt: Order the documentation of defects found during a manhole inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: inspection found infiltration at a joint, a cracked bench, and roots at the incoming pipe of a residential manhole.

cards.label: Assess whether any defect is an immediate hazard, such as a displaced frame or missing step, and arrange barriers or urgent repair if so
Photograph each defect with a location reference in the frame before any cleaning or disturbance
Complete the condition rating and recommended action for each defect, such as monitor, seal, or rehabilitate
Estimate and record any infiltration rate in descriptive terms, such as weeper, dripper, or runner, and note if flow is clear groundwater
Record the defect type, location by clock position and depth from the cover, and severity on the inspection form
Submit the form and photographs to the work order system the same day and note the manhole asset number on every record

tasks.explanation: Photographs come before disturbance so the evidence is true. Location, type, and severity make the record findable and comparable, hazards are acted on immediately, and same day submission with the asset number links the condition to the maintenance system.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps after a manhole inspection finds the cover and frame broken and sitting below road grade.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: arterial road manhole, frame cracked, cover rocking and 40 mm low, traffic is passing over it.

cards.label: Raise an urgent work order for frame and cover replacement and adjustment to grade
Record the measurements, photographs, and road condition details for the repair crew and the asset record
Arrange temporary measures directed by the supervisor, such as a steel plate or cold patch ramp, installed by the road crew
Confirm the temporary measure is secure and traffic can pass safely before removing barriers
Record the hazard, temporary measure, and work order number in the inspection log and flag the location for follow up inspection
Protect the location immediately with cones and barriers and notify the supervisor of a road hazard

tasks.explanation: Public protection comes before paperwork when traffic is hitting a broken frame. Measurements and the urgent work order follow, the temporary measure is proven secure before barriers come off, and follow up is flagged because a plated manhole is not a finished repair.

tasks.prompt: Order a wet weather manhole check for infiltration at the joints and connections.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: during steady rain, crew checks a manhole with known joint infiltration to gauge its severity for the rehabilitation program.

cards.label: Inspect each joint, pipe connection, and the chimney in turn and identify which are leaking and which are dry
Confirm it is raining steadily and record rainfall and the time the check starts, so the observation represents wet weather response
Photograph the active leaks and note whether the water is clear, which supports groundwater infiltration rather than surface inflow
Open the manhole safely with traffic control, ventilation, and testing, and allow flow conditions to settle after opening
Classify each leak as a weeper, dripper, or runner and estimate the combined inflow contribution
Record the findings against the asset number and update the rehabilitation priority with the wet weather evidence

tasks.explanation: Wet weather evidence is only valid if the rain conditions are documented. Systematic joint by joint inspection separates sources, classification gives a comparable severity, and clear water distinguishes infiltration from inflow for the rehabilitation decision.

tasks.prompt: Order the pre-rehabilitation assessment of a manhole selected for lining or sealing.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: manhole is a candidate for rehabilitation, assessment must confirm it is suitable and what preparation is needed.

cards.label: Inspect the structure from the surface for soundness of the walls, benching, and channel, and confirm it is not structurally failed
Measure the internal dimensions, depth, and pipe sizes and confirm access for rehabilitation equipment
Record the suitability decision, measurements, and preparation list in the rehabilitation file for the contractor
Confirm bypass or flow control needs during the work based on the flows observed and the time of day planned
Review the inspection history, CCTV records for connected pipes, and the reason the manhole was selected
Identify preparation needs such as cleaning, root removal, infiltration control, and bench or channel repairs

tasks.explanation: History explains why the structure was chosen. Soundness decides suitability because lining a failed structure wastes the work, measurements and preparation define the job, and flow control planning protects the work window.

tasks.prompt: Order the preparation for a confined space entry into a lift station wet well for pump work.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: planned entry into a wet well classified as a confined space, Ontario confined space requirements apply, entry team of entrant, attendant, and supervisor.

cards.label: Isolate the space by stopping inflow where possible, locking out pumps and electrical sources, and blanking or tagging valves as planned
Authorize the entry on the permit, post the attendant at the opening with the log, and begin entry with continuous monitoring
Set up the tripod or retrieval system, harness, ventilation blower, and communication equipment and inspect each item
Ventilate the space and retest to confirm acceptable conditions, then brief the entrant and attendant on duties and rescue arrangements
Calibrate or bump test the gas detector and test the atmosphere before entry in the required gas order
Complete the hazard assessment and entry permit for the specific wet well and task before any setup

tasks.explanation: Paperwork and isolation come before equipment, because the permit defines what must be controlled. Equipment is inspected before testing, testing precedes ventilation decisions and retesting, and authorization plus a posted attendant immediately precede entry.

tasks.prompt: Order the atmospheric testing sequence at a confined space opening before entry.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: four gas detector, testing a wet well from the top before entry, probe lowered on a line to different depths.

cards.label: Test the atmosphere at the opening first, before any worker leans over or into the space
Lower the probe to test at several depths, including the bottom and just above the liquid surface, allowing response time at each level
Compare all readings with the entry limits on the permit and record them with times on the permit
Test for oxygen first, then flammable gases and vapours, then toxic gases including hydrogen sulfide and carbon monoxide
If any reading is outside limits, withdraw, ventilate, and retest the full sequence before reconsidering entry
Confirm the detector is calibrated and passes a fresh air zero and bump test at the surface before use

tasks.explanation: A proven detector and a first test at the opening protect the tester. The gas order matters because oxygen affects the flammable reading and both precede toxics, testing at depth finds stratified gases, and out of limit results restart the process with ventilation.

tasks.prompt: Order the ventilation setup for a confined space entry into a sewer manhole for inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, the permit system where it applies, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: entry manhole on a large trunk sewer, blower and duct available, entry follows Ontario confined space practice.

cards.label: Test the atmosphere at all levels with ventilation running and confirm readings are within entry limits
Position the blower upwind of the opening in fresh air so it cannot draw in vehicle exhaust or sewer gas
Start ventilation and run it long enough to exchange the air in the space before testing for entry
Keep ventilation running continuously during the entry and position the duct so it does not block the retrieval path
Run the duct to the bottom of the space so fresh air reaches the lowest level where gases collect
If ventilation stops during entry, the entrant exits immediately and the full test sequence is repeated before re-entry

tasks.explanation: Blower placement in clean air and ducting to the bottom come first, because ventilating the top only leaves heavy gases below. Testing is done with ventilation running as it will be during entry, and a ventilation failure means exit and a full retest.
